newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Dubrovacka Banka '96 pre-tax HRK 18.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Dubrovacka Banka '96 pre-tax HRK 18.6 mln.

text.p: Croatian Dubrovacka Banka on Thursday reported a 18.6 million kuna pre-tax profit for last year after higher risk provisions, down from 57.2 million profit in 1995.

"After all the adversities that have been present for the full six years Dubrovacka Banka did very well in 1996, maintaining a considerable growth trend that began in 1995," it said in an annual report published in daily Slobodna Dalmacija.
It referred to a war-induced slump of the tourist trade and related businesses that once fuelled the economy of the southern coastal region where Dubrovacka is based.
The bank proposed a dividend of six percent on the face value of its bearer shares, without giving comparison for 1995.
Total 1996 income rose 88 percent to 325 million kuna, with operating profit almost trebled at 166.2 million, it said.
This enabled the bank to set aside 147.5 million kuna for loan provisions, raising total provisions to 387 million kuna.
New risk provisions rose from only 200,000 kuna in 1995.
"That significantly strengthened funds and increased the protection against any kind of risk," the bank added.
Continuing a policy of growth, the bank opened new branches and retail outlets outside the Dubrovnik-Neretva county in an attempt to boost business with citizens and entrepreneurs.
Overall deposits jumped 106.5 percent to 1.2 billion kuna last year, creating conditions to increase loans, it said.
It put the capital to risk asset ratio at 12.78 percent, but there were no details of the credit activity last year.
The bank's balance sheet expanded to 2.2 billion kuna from 1.5 billion kuna at the end of 1995.

"By channelling income into reserves and increasing the shareholder capital, the bank's stability and the level of its own funds were boosted, forming a basis for even more favourable results in 1997," Dubrovacka said.
Its 472 million kuna total reserves, including the legal requirement, represented coverage for 26 percent of all placements, it said.
Shareholders' capital stood at 11.20 percent of its assets last year, but the bank gave no comparison for 1995. It ranked 12th on a list of Croatian banks according to capital in 1995.
Dubrovacka is listed in a parallel segment of the Zagreb Stock Exchange but its stock is not traded. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
